items.reason: Clear membership rule with obvious NVIDIA/AMD/Intel codenames and a deep tail of mobile, workstation, and historical GPU architectures.
Well-bounded category with immediate answers like Verilog and VHDL plus a solid tail of modern embedded and academic HDLs.
Fun, accessible category with instant classics (Caesar, Enigma) and a rich tail of classical and mechanical ciphers.
Crisp decade boundary with iconic 80s micros up front and a huge international tail of obscure home computers.
Every developer knows KVM, VirtualBox, and ESXi, and there is a real tail of research, embedded, and cloud hypervisors.
Clear vendor-scoped CPU codename list with familiar modern cores and a deep tail of older, Atom, and server microarchitectures.
Cleanly defined set of named network/NoC topologies with decent depth from mesh and torus to fat-tree, Clos, and Kautz.
Too few distinct named KDFs beyond PBKDF2, scrypt, Argon2, bcrypt, and HKDF to sustain a deep tail.
Most programmers only know the 7-8 basic Boolean gates, and the tail of reversible/quantum/async gates is too small.
Famous worms and ransomware give strong obvious answers, backed by a massive, well-documented tail of APTs and malware families.
Strong mix of everyday acronyms (DRAM, SRAM, flash) and fascinating historical/emerging memory technologies.
Classic 8086/6502/Z80 answers come to mind immediately, with a huge historical and modern catalog of commercial CPUs.
Clear security-domain category with well-known tools like Nmap and Metasploit plus a deep red-team and Kali ecosystem.
Narrower than expected once signatures and key exchange are excluded, leaving too few well-known named schemes.
Crisp hardware category with obvious x86/ARM answers (SSE, AVX, NEON) and a solid tail across Power, MIPS, SPARC, and RISC-V.
Well-bounded historical category with iconic Cray and Connection Machine entries and a rich supercomputing tail.
Hyper-niche specification API names that almost no general developer can recall offhand.
Exact official list of laureates with famous CS pioneers up front and a rewarding deep tail.
Obscure firmware specification interface names with virtually zero obvious answers for ordinary programmers.
Instant nostalgic hits (PlayStation, N64, Saturn) paired with a fun tail of obscure 90s consoles and handhelds.
